### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. complement component 3 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.488)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGB2 (HGNC:6109) —DISRUPTS→ integrin activation for leukocyte adhesion (GO:0007155); integrin activation for leukocyte adhesion (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ impaired leukocyte adhesion (HP:0011077); C3 (HGNC:246) —DISRUPTS→ complement system activation (GO:0006955); complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0012339); complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ impaired opsonization (HP:0002710); impaired leukocyte adhesion (HP:0011077) —DECREASES→ complement system activation (GO:0006955); impaired opsonization (HP:0002710) —DECREASES→ impaired leukocyte adhesion (HP:0011077). Loss-of-function mutations in ITGB2 impair integrin activation, leading to impaired leukocyte adhesion. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in C3 disrupt the complement cascade, resulting in impaired opsonization and recurrent bacterial infections. The impaired leukocyte adhesion and complement activation converge on reduced ability of the immune system to effectively clear pathogens.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic evidence shows that mutations in ITGB2 do not impair leukocyte adhesion or that mutations in C3 do not affect complement activation and opsonization, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 0.01) in the gnomAD database in either ITGB2 or C3 that is associated with normal immune function.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap can inform therapeutic strategies for recurrent infections in LAD1 by potentially targeting complement-mediated pathways, and vice versa, by exploring how improved leukocyte adhesion might mitigate some C3 deficiency-related consequences. This highlights the interconnectedness of innate immune mechanisms.
